atoms.b: Weather refers to the short term, day-to-day changes in conditions. For example, it could be ((++sunny dirty)) today and ((++rainy sleepy)) tomorrow.
To understand the weather, we must also consider the temperature, or how hot or ((++cold dark)) it is. We can measure temperature using a device called a ((++thermometer telescope)).

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: We rely on weather forecasts to predict what the weather conditions will be like over the coming days. An organisation called the Met Office is responsible for creating UK weather forecasts.
Weather can be predicted in many different ways. One way is through measuring ground conditions, such as air pressure as well as wind speed and direction.
Weather can also be predicted in the atmosphere, through satellites and instruments that use radar.

atoms.a: What organisation is responsible for predicting weather forecasts in the UK?
Which two ground conditions can help us predict the weather?
Which two methods are used to measure conditions in the atmosphere?
